title: The 30-millisecond escape
summary: Find the wire that gets a fly out from under a swatter.

steps.text: A swatter swoops at the fly. Tap Stimulate to fire the looming neurons (the swatter spotters).
steps.result: They fire, and in a few thousandths of a second the giant fiber (the escape wire) fires too.

steps.text: Tap Stimulate again. Follow the giant fiber (the escape wire) down into the nerve cord (its spinal cord).
steps.result: The jump neurons (the leg kickers) fire within 30 milliseconds. They kick the middle legs, and the fly leaps away.

steps.text: Now silence the giant fiber (the escape wire). We will send the swatter. Watch the jump neurons (the leg kickers).
steps.result: The looming neurons (the swatter spotters) still fire, but the jump neurons stay dark. The fast escape is gone.

steps.text: Tap the giant fiber (the escape wire) button again to switch it back on. We will send the same swatter.
steps.result: The jump neurons (the leg kickers) fire again. Real flies also have slower ways out, but this is the fastest.

check.question: You silenced the giant fiber (the escape wire). Why did the leg kickers stay dark?

choices.text: The fly never saw the swatter.
choices.feedback: Not quite. The blue swatter spotters still fired, so the fly saw it. The signal stopped at the escape wire.

choices.text: The escape wire carries the jump signal to the leg kickers.
choices.feedback: Yes! The swatter spotters tell the escape wire, and the escape wire tells the legs to jump. Cut the wire and the fast jump is gone.

choices.text: You switched off the leg kickers too.
choices.feedback: Not quite. You only silenced the escape wire. The leg kickers stayed on but got no signal.

freePlay.title: Free play
freePlay.text: Every button works now. Guess first, then tap: which colors still light up with the escape wire silenced? Then try silencing the swatter spotters instead.
